#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import json
import base64
import io
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv', parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])

# Clean price_pence (float in source, cast to float)
df['price_pence'] = pd.to_numeric(df['price_pence'], errors='coerce')

# Drop rows with null price or timestamps
df = df.dropna(subset=['price_pence', 'recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])

# Compute update lag in hours (recorded_at − source_updated_at)
df['lag_hours'] = (df['recorded_at'] - df['source_updated_at']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

# Fuel type canonical ordering
FUEL_LABELS = {'E10': 'E10 (Std Unleaded)', 'B7_STANDARD': 'B7 (Std Diesel)', 'E5': 'E5 (Super Unleaded)'}
FUEL_ORDER   = ['E10', 'B7_STANDARD', 'E5']
FUEL_COLORS  = {'E10': '#2563EB', 'B7_STANDARD': '#16A34A', 'E5': '#DC2626'}

fuel_types = [f for f in FUEL_ORDER if f in df['fuel_type'].unique()]
other_types = [f for f in df['fuel_type'].unique() if f not in FUEL_ORDER]
all_types = fuel_types + other_types

# ── Global KPIs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
total_records    = len(df)
unique_stations  = df['node_id'].nunique()
date_min         = df['recorded_at'].min()
date_max         = df['recorded_at'].max()
source_min       = df['source_updated_at'].min()
source_max       = df['source_updated_at'].max()
fuel_type_counts = df['fuel_type'].value_counts().to_dict()

# ── Price statistics by fuel type ──────────────────────────────────────────────
price_stats = {}
for ft in all_types:
    sub = df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence']
    price_stats[ft] = {
        'count':  len(sub),
        'mean':   sub.mean(),
        'median': sub.median(),
        'std':    sub.std(),
        'min':    sub.min(),
        'max':    sub.max(),
        'p25':    sub.quantile(0.25),
        'p75':    sub.quantile(0.75),
        'iqr':    sub.quantile(0.75) - sub.quantile(0.25),
        'spread': sub.max() - sub.min(),
    }

# ── Update lag statistics ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Remove negative lags (data artefacts) and extreme outliers for analysis
lag_clean = df[df['lag_hours'] >= 0]['lag_hours']
neg_lag_count = (df['lag_hours'] < 0).sum()

lag_stats = {
    'total_records_with_lag': len(lag_clean),
    'neg_lag_count': int(neg_lag_count),
    'neg_lag_pct':   neg_lag_count / len(df) * 100,
    'median_hours':  lag_clean.median(),
    'mean_hours':    lag_clean.mean(),
    'p25_hours':     lag_clean.quantile(0.25),
    'p75_hours':     lag_clean.quantile(0.75),
    'p90_hours':     lag_clean.quantile(0.90),
    'p95_hours':     lag_clean.quantile(0.95),
    'max_hours':     lag_clean.max(),
}

# Lag buckets
buckets = {
    '< 1 hour':    (lag_clean < 1).sum(),
    '1–6 hours':   ((lag_clean >= 1) & (lag_clean < 6)).sum(),
    '6–24 hours':  ((lag_clean >= 6) & (lag_clean < 24)).sum(),
    '1–7 days':    ((lag_clean >= 24) & (lag_clean < 168)).sum(),
    '7–30 days':   ((lag_clean >= 168) & (lag_clean < 720)).sum(),
    '> 30 days':   (lag_clean >= 720).sum(),
}

# ── Station coverage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
station_fuels = df.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].nunique()
coverage_counts = station_fuels.value_counts().sort_index()

fuel_station_counts = df.groupby('fuel_type')['node_id'].nunique()

# Per-station fuel set
station_fuel_sets = df.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].apply(set)

# ── Helper: fig to base64 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def fig_to_b64(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode()
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64

# ── Chart 1: Box plots — price by fuel type ───────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
box_data  = [df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence'].dropna().values for ft in fuel_types]
box_labels = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft) for ft in fuel_types]
colors = [FUEL_COLORS[ft] for ft in fuel_types]

bp = ax.boxplot(box_data, patch_artist=True, notch=False, vert=True,
                medianprops=dict(color='white', linewidth=2.5),
                whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2, alpha=0.3, linestyle='none'))
for patch, color in zip(bp['boxes'], colors):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
    patch.set_alpha(0.8)
for whisker, cap in zip(bp['whiskers'], bp['caps']):
    whisker.set_color('#555')
    cap.set_color('#555')

ax.set_xticklabels(box_labels, fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.35, linestyle='--')
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
for i, ft in enumerate(fuel_types, 1):
    s = price_stats[ft]
    ax.annotate(f"Med: {s['median']:.1f}p", xy=(i, s['median']),
                xytext=(i + 0.3, s['median']),
                fontsize=8.5, color='#333', va='center')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_boxplot = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 2: Mean + IQR bar chart ────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
x = np.arange(len(fuel_types))
means   = [price_stats[ft]['mean']   for ft in fuel_types]
medians = [price_stats[ft]['median'] for ft in fuel_types]
p25s    = [price_stats[ft]['p25']    for ft in fuel_types]
p75s    = [price_stats[ft]['p75']    for ft in fuel_types]

bars = ax.bar(x, means, color=[FUEL_COLORS[ft] for ft in fuel_types],
              alpha=0.85, width=0.45, zorder=3)
# IQR error bars
for i, ft in enumerate(fuel_types):
    ax.plot([i, i], [p25s[i], p75s[i]], color='#333', linewidth=2.5, zorder=4)
    ax.plot([i - 0.1, i + 0.1], [p25s[i], p25s[i]], color='#333', linewidth=1.5, zorder=4)
    ax.plot([i - 0.1, i + 0.1], [p75s[i], p75s[i]], color='#333', linewidth=1.5, zorder=4)
    ax.text(i, means[i] + 0.5, f'{means[i]:.1f}p', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels([FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft) for ft in fuel_types], fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Mean Price with IQR by Fuel Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.35, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.set_ylim(min(p25s) - 5, max([price_stats[ft]['max'] for ft in fuel_types]) + 5)

# Legend for IQR marker
iqr_line = mpatches.Patch(color='#333', label='IQR (25th–75th pct)')
ax.legend(handles=[iqr_line], fontsize=9, loc='upper right')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_mean_iqr = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 3: Price spread (max-min) ──────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
spreads = [price_stats[ft]['spread'] for ft in fuel_types]
iqrs    = [price_stats[ft]['iqr']    for ft in fuel_types]
labels  = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)  for ft in fuel_types]
x = np.arange(len(fuel_types))
w = 0.35
ax.bar(x - w/2, spreads, width=w, color='#DC2626', alpha=0.8, label='Max − Min (Full Spread)', zorder=3)
ax.bar(x + w/2, iqrs,    width=w, color='#2563EB', alpha=0.8, label='IQR (P25–P75)',           zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Pence per litre', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Spread & Market Competitiveness by Fuel Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.35, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
for i, (s, iq) in enumerate(zip(spreads, iqrs)):
    ax.text(i - w/2, s + 0.3, f'{s:.1f}p', ha='center', fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', color='#DC2626')
    ax.text(i + w/2, iq + 0.3, f'{iq:.1f}p', ha='center', fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', color='#2563EB')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_spread = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 4: Update lag distribution (log-scale histogram) ───────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.5))
bins = [0, 0.5, 1, 2, 6, 12, 24, 48, 72, 168, 336, 720, 2000]
bin_labels = ['<30m', '30m-1h', '1-2h', '2-6h', '6-12h', '12-24h',
              '1-2d', '2-3d', '3-7d', '7-14d', '14-30d', '>30d']
counts_hist = [((lag_clean >= bins[i]) & (lag_clean < bins[i+1])).sum() for i in range(len(bins)-1)]
colors_hist = ['#16A34A' if i <= 1 else '#F59E0B' if i <= 5 else '#DC2626' for i in range(len(bin_labels))]
bars = ax.bar(range(len(bin_labels)), counts_hist, color=colors_hist, alpha=0.85, zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(bin_labels)))
ax.set_xticklabels(bin_labels, rotation=35, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Records', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Distribution of Price Update Lag (source_updated_at → recorded_at)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.35, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'{int(x):,}'))

# legend
patches = [
    mpatches.Patch(color='#16A34A', label='≤ 1 hour (fresh)'),
    mpatches.Patch(color='#F59E0B', label='1 h – 24 h'),
    mpatches.Patch(color='#DC2626', label='> 24 hours (stale)')
]
ax.legend(handles=patches, fontsize=9)
fig.tight_layout()
chart_lag_hist = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 5: Lag bucket pie ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
bucket_labels = list(buckets.keys())
bucket_vals   = list(buckets.values())
pie_colors = ['#16A34A', '#22C55E', '#F59E0B', '#EF4444', '#DC2626', '#991B1B']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
    bucket_vals, labels=bucket_labels, autopct='%1.1f%%',
    colors=pie_colors, startangle=140, pctdistance=0.82,
    textprops={'fontsize': 9.5}
)
for at in autotexts:
    at.set_fontsize(9)
ax.set_title('Update Lag Breakdown by Time Window', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
fig.tight_layout()
chart_lag_pie = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 6: Station fuel coverage ───────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
cov_x = coverage_counts.index.tolist()
cov_y = coverage_counts.values.tolist()
colors_cov = ['#60A5FA', '#2563EB', '#1E3A8A'][:len(cov_x)]
bars = ax.bar([str(c) for c in cov_x], cov_y, color=colors_cov, alpha=0.85, zorder=3)
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Fuel Types Reported', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Stations', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Station Coverage by Fuel Type Breadth', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.35, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'{int(x):,}'))
for bar, val in zip(bars, cov_y):
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 10,
            f'{val:,}', ha='center', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_coverage = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 7: Fuel type by station count ─────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
ft_labels = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft) for ft in fuel_types]
ft_counts = [fuel_station_counts.get(ft, 0) for ft in fuel_types]
bars = ax.barh(ft_labels, ft_counts, color=[FUEL_COLORS[ft] for ft in fuel_types], alpha=0.85)
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Unique Stations', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Station Count by Fuel Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.xaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.35, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'{int(x):,}'))
for bar, val in zip(bars, ft_counts):
    ax.text(val + 20, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'{val:,}', va='center', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_fuel_stations = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 8: Percentile profile per fuel type (line) ─────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
pcts = [5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95]
for ft in fuel_types:
    sub = df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence']
    vals = [sub.quantile(p/100) for p in pcts]
    ax.plot(pcts, vals, marker='o', label=FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft),
            color=FUEL_COLORS[ft], linewidth=2, markersize=5)
ax.set_xlabel('Percentile', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Percentile Profile by Fuel Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
ax.xaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.25, linestyle='--')
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.35, linestyle='--')
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
ax.set_xticks(pcts)
ax.set_xticklabels([f'P{p}' for p in pcts])
fig.tight_layout()
chart_percentile = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Print summary for debug ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
print(f"Records: {total_records:,}  |  Stations: {unique_stations:,}")
print(f"Fuel types: {list(fuel_type_counts.keys())}")

print("Lag buckets:", {k: int(v) for k, v in buckets.items()})
print("Coverage:", coverage_counts.to_dict())

def pct(n, total): return f"{n/total*100:.1f}%"

def fp(v): return f"{v:.1f}"  # 1dp

<div class="page">

<!-- ══ COVER ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

<!-- ══ SECTION 1: DATASET OVERVIEW ═══════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">01</span>
    <span class="section-title">Dataset Overview & Coverage Summary</span>
  </div>

  <p>This analysis draws on <strong>{total_records:,} price observations</strong> collected from
  <strong>{unique_stations:,} unique UK forecourts</strong> under the government-mandated Fuel Finder
  open data scheme. Data was compiled by fuelcosts.co.uk and covers prices recorded between
  <strong>{date_min.strftime('%d %b %Y')}</strong> and <strong>{date_max.strftime('%d %b %Y')}</strong>.
  Retailer price updates span from <strong>{source_min.strftime('%d %b %Y')}</strong> to
  <strong>{source_max.strftime('%d %b %Y')}</strong>.</p>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Fuel Type</th>
        <th>Records</th>
        <th>% of Total</th>
        <th>Unique Stations</th>
        <th>Station Coverage</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for ft in all_types:
    label = FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)
    rec   = fuel_type_counts.get(ft, 0)
    sta   = fuel_station_counts.get(ft, 0)
    pct_r = rec / total_records * 100
    pct_s = sta / unique_stations * 100
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{label}</td>
        <td>{rec:,}</td>
        <td>{pct_r:.1f}%</td>
        <td>{sta:,}</td>
        <td>{pct_s:.1f}%</td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="callout callout-info">
    <span class="callout-icon">ℹ️</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Data Completeness:</strong> Station identifiers are anonymised SHA-style hashes. Individual station
      names, brands, or geographic locations cannot be determined from this dataset alone, limiting geographic or
      brand-level sub-analysis. No structural null values were detected across the core analytical columns
      (price_pence, recorded_at, source_updated_at). Price values are in whole or decimal pence per litre.
      {f'<strong>Note:</strong> {lag_stats["neg_lag_count"]:,} records ({lag_stats["neg_lag_pct"]:.1f}%) show a negative update lag (source_updated_at > recorded_at), suggesting minor clock-skew or data ingestion artefacts; these are excluded from lag analysis.' if lag_stats['neg_lag_count'] > 0 else ''}
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ══ SECTION 2: PRICE DISTRIBUTION ═════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">02</span>
    <span class="section-title">Price Distribution by Fuel Type</span>
  </div>

  <p>The box plots and summary statistics below characterise the full distribution of retail prices
  for each fuel type across all reporting stations. Diesel (B7 Standard) commands the highest average
  price, while E5 Super Unleaded — despite a lower record count — shows notable inter-station spread.</p>

  <div class="chart-row cols-2">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_boxplot}" alt="Box plots of price distribution by fuel type">
      <div class="chart-caption">Box plots showing median, IQR, whiskers (1.5×IQR), and outliers for each fuel type</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_mean_iqr}" alt="Mean price with IQR bars by fuel type">
      <div class="chart-caption">Mean price per fuel type; vertical bars indicate IQR (25th–75th percentile range)</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Fuel Type</th>
        <th>Records</th>
        <th>Mean (p/L)</th>

        <th>P75</th>
        <th>Max</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>

"""
for ft in all_types:
    s     = price_stats[ft]
    label = FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{label}</td>
        <td>{s['count']:,}</td>
        <td><strong>{fp(s['mean'])}</strong></td>

        <td>{fp(s['std'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['min'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['p25'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['p75'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['max'])}</td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-row cols-1">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_percentile}" alt="Price percentile profile by fuel type">
      <div class="chart-caption">Percentile profile (P5–P95) illustrating the shape of the price distribution for each fuel type</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <h3>Key Observations</h3>
  <div class="stat-row">
    <div class="stat-pill">E10 mean: <strong>{fp(price_stats['E10']['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">B7 Diesel mean: <strong>{fp(price_stats['B7_STANDARD']['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
    {'<div class="stat-pill">E5 mean: <strong>' + fp(price_stats['E5']['mean']) + 'p/L</strong></div>' if 'E5' in price_stats else ''}
    <div class="stat-pill">Diesel premium over E10: <strong>{fp(price_stats['B7_STANDARD']['mean'] - price_stats['E10']['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
  </div>
  <p>The standard deviation for E10 ({fp(price_stats['E10']['std'])}p/L) and B7 ({fp(price_stats['B7_STANDARD']['std'])}p/L)
  reflects genuine inter-station price variation rather than measurement noise, consistent with imperfect competition
  across forecourts.</p>
</div>

<!-- ══ SECTION 3: PRICE SPREAD & COMPETITIVENESS ════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">03</span>
    <span class="section-title">Price Spread & Market Competitiveness</span>
  </div>

  <p>Market competitiveness is assessed through two metrics: the <strong>full price spread</strong>
  (maximum minus minimum price) indicating the widest possible consumer disparity, and the
  <strong>IQR</strong> (interquartile range) indicating the typical price band that the majority
  of consumers encounter.</p>

  <div class="chart-row cols-1">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_spread}" alt="Price spread and IQR by fuel type">
      <div class="chart-caption">Red bars: full price spread (max − min); blue bars: IQR (P25–P75). Both in pence per litre.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Fuel Type</th>
        <th>Min (p/L)</th>
        <th>Max (p/L)</th>
        <th>Spread (p/L)</th>
        <th>P25 (p/L)</th>
        <th>P75 (p/L)</th>
        <th>IQR (p/L)</th>
        <th>Competitiveness</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for ft in all_types:
    s     = price_stats[ft]
    label = FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)
    # Simple competitiveness flag based on IQR
    if s['iqr'] <= 4:
        comp_badge = '<span class="badge badge-green">Competitive</span>'
    elif s['iqr'] <= 8:
        comp_badge = '<span class="badge badge-amber">Moderate</span>'
    else:
        comp_badge = '<span class="badge badge-red">Wide Spread</span>'
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{label}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['min'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['max'])}</td>
        <td><strong>{fp(s['spread'])}</strong></td>
        <td>{fp(s['p25'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['p75'])}</td>
        <td><strong>{fp(s['iqr'])}</strong></td>
        <td>{comp_badge}</td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="callout callout-warn">
    <span class="callout-icon">⚠️</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Consumer Impact:</strong> A spread of {fp(price_stats['E10']['spread'])}p/L for E10 means that for a
      typical 50-litre fill, consumers at the most expensive stations pay approximately
      <strong>£{price_stats['E10']['spread']*50/100:.2f} more</strong> than those at the cheapest forecourt.
      The IQR of {fp(price_stats['E10']['iqr'])}p/L implies that moving between the 25th and 75th percentile
      stations saves <strong>£{price_stats['E10']['iqr']*50/100:.2f}</strong> per fill — a meaningful incentive for price-aware shopping.
    </div>
  </div>

  <p>The IQR is the more policy-relevant metric: it describes the price variation that the majority of consumers
  face in practice, filtering out extreme outliers at either end of the market. An IQR above ~5p/L suggests
  meaningful consumer disparity; values below ~3p/L are indicative of a highly competitive market.</p>
</div>

<!-- ══ SECTION 4: UPDATE FRESHNESS ══════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">04</span>
    <span class="section-title">Retailer Reporting Freshness Analysis</span>
  </div>

  <p>Update freshness is measured as the lag between <code>source_updated_at</code> (when the retailer
  reported the price to the government feed) and <code>recorded_at</code> (when the data collection
  system captured it). A low lag indicates timely reporting; high lags suggest stale data that may
  not reflect actual pump prices consumers encounter.</p>

  <div class="chart-row cols-2">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_lag_hist}" alt="Update lag distribution histogram">
      <div class="chart-caption">Distribution of update lags across all records (green: ≤1h fresh; amber: 1–24h; red: >24h stale)</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_lag_pie}" alt="Update lag breakdown pie chart">
      <div class="chart-caption">Proportion of records by lag time window</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Lag Window</th>
        <th>Record Count</th>
        <th>% of Records</th>
        <th>Assessment</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
"""
assessments = {
    '< 1 hour':   ('badge-green',  'Fresh — near real-time'),
    '1–6 hours':  ('badge-green',  'Fresh — same day'),
    '6–24 hours': ('badge-amber',  'Acceptable — within 24h'),
    '1–7 days':   ('badge-amber',  'Marginal — 1 to 7 days'),
    '7–30 days':  ('badge-red',    'Stale — 7 to 30 days'),
    '> 30 days':  ('badge-red',    'Very stale — over 30 days'),
}
total_lag_recs = sum(buckets.values())
for k, v in buckets.items():
    badge_cls, assess = assessments[k]
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{k}</td>
        <td>{int(v):,}</td>
        <td>{v/total_lag_recs*100:.1f}%</td>
        <td><span class="badge {badge_cls}">{assess}</span></td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="stat-row">
    <div class="stat-pill">Median lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['median_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">Mean lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['mean_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">P90 lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['p90_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">P95 lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['p95_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">Max lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['max_hours'])}h</strong></div>
  </div>

  {'<div class="callout callout-warn"><span class="callout-icon">⚠️</span><div class="callout-text"><strong>Negative Lag Artefacts:</strong> ' + f"{lag_stats['neg_lag_count']:,} records ({lag_stats['neg_lag_pct']:.1f}%)" + ' show a negative update lag (source_updated_at later than recorded_at). This likely reflects minor clock-skew between the government API and the collection system, or records updated retroactively. These records have been excluded from lag analysis above.</div></div>' if lag_stats['neg_lag_count'] > 0 else ''}

  <p>The skew between mean ({fp(lag_stats['mean_hours'])}h) and median ({fp(lag_stats['median_hours'])}h) lag indicates
  a long right tail: while the majority of records are updated promptly, a subset of stations have very infrequent
  updates, inflating the mean. Regulators should focus compliance monitoring on the tail — stations contributing
  to the P90+ lag population — rather than average behaviour.</p>
</div>

<!-- ══ SECTION 5: STATION COVERAGE ══════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">05</span>
    <span class="section-title">Station Coverage & Fuel Type Availability</span>
  </div>

      <div class="chart-caption">Distribution of stations by the number of fuel types they report</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_fuel_stations}" alt="Station count by fuel type">

    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Fuel Types Reported</th>
        <th>Station Count</th>
        <th>% of Stations</th>
        <th>Note</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for n_fuels, count in coverage_counts.items():
    pct_s = count / unique_stations * 100
    note  = "Reporting all 3 main types" if n_fuels == 3 else "Partial reporters — may sell premium diesel/E5 not captured" if n_fuels == 2 else "Single fuel reporters — likely specialist or incomplete data"
    HTML += f"""      <tr>

      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Fuel Type</th>
        <th>Stations Reporting</th>
        <th>% of Total Stations</th>
        <th>Reach</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for ft in all_types:
    label  = FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)
    sta    = fuel_station_counts.get(ft, 0)
    pct_s  = sta / unique_stations * 100
    if pct_s >= 70:
        reach = '<span class="badge badge-green">Broad</span>'
    elif pct_s >= 40:
        reach = '<span class="badge badge-amber">Moderate</span>'
    else:
        reach = '<span class="badge badge-red">Limited</span>'
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{label}</td>
        <td>{sta:,}</td>
        <td>{pct_s:.1f}%</td>
        <td>{reach}</td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="callout callout-info">
    <span class="callout-icon">ℹ️</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Geographic limitation:</strong> Station-level geographic metadata (address, brand, region) is not
      available in this dataset. Consequently, coverage gaps cannot be mapped to specific regions or retailer
      networks. A join to the UK Fuel Finder station registry would be required for spatial analysis.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Its narrower station coverage (' + fp(fuel_station_counts.get('E5', 0) / unique_stations * 100) + '% of stations) and the premium nature of the product may limit competitive pressure, contributing to wider price dispersion.' if 'E5' in price_stats else 'E5 data, where present, shows pricing at a premium to E10 consistent with its higher-octane specification.'}</div>

python3 -c "
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv', parse_dates=['recorded_at','source_updated_at'])
df['price_pence'] = pd.to_numeric(df['price_pence'], errors='coerce')

# Apply IQR-based outlier filter per fuel type
def clean(sub):
    q1, q3 = sub['price_pence'].quantile([0.01, 0.99])
    return sub[(sub['price_pence'] >= q1) & (sub['price_pence'] <= q3)]

df_c = df.groupby('fuel_type', group_keys=False).apply(clean)
print('After filter:')
for ft, sub in df_c.groupby('fuel_type'):
    p = sub['price_pence']
    print(f'{ft}: n={len(p)} mean={p.mean():.2f} median={p.median():.2f} min={p.min():.1f} max={p.max():.1f} IQR={p.quantile(.75)-p.quantile(.25):.2f}')
print('Total:', len(df_c), '/', len(df))
"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import base64
import io
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Load & clean ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df_raw = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv', parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])
df_raw['price_pence'] = pd.to_numeric(df_raw['price_pence'], errors='coerce')
df_raw = df_raw.dropna(subset=['price_pence', 'recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])

total_records_raw = len(df_raw)

# P1/P99 clip per fuel type to remove obvious data errors (e.g. 1879p/L)
def clip_outliers(sub):
    q1, q99 = sub['price_pence'].quantile([0.01, 0.99])
    return sub[(sub['price_pence'] >= q1) & (sub['price_pence'] <= q99)]

df = df_raw.groupby('fuel_type', group_keys=False).apply(
    lambda x: clip_outliers(x)
).reset_index(drop=True)

outlier_count = total_records_raw - len(df)

# ── Fuel type order & labels ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
FUEL_ORDER = ['E10', 'B7_STANDARD', 'E5', 'B7_PREMIUM', 'HVO', 'B10']
FUEL_LABELS = {
    'E10':        'E10 (Std Unleaded)',
    'B7_STANDARD':'B7 (Std Diesel)',
    'E5':         'E5 (Super Unleaded)',
    'B7_PREMIUM': 'B7 Premium Diesel',
    'HVO':        'HVO (Renewable)',
    'B10':        'B10 (Bio-diesel)',
}
FUEL_COLORS = {
    'E10':        '#2563EB',
    'B7_STANDARD':'#16A34A',
    'E5':         '#7C3AED',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#EA580C',
    'HVO':        '#0891B2',
    'B10':        '#CA8A04',
}

present_types = [f for f in FUEL_ORDER if f in df['fuel_type'].unique()]
other_types   = [f for f in df['fuel_type'].unique() if f not in FUEL_ORDER]
all_types     = present_types + other_types

# Main 3 for box plots (sufficient records)
MAIN_TYPES = [f for f in ['E10', 'B7_STANDARD', 'E5'] if f in all_types]
PREM_TYPES = [f for f in ['B7_PREMIUM', 'HVO', 'B10'] if f in all_types]

# ── Global KPIs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
total_records   = len(df_raw)
unique_stations = df_raw['node_id'].nunique()
date_min        = df_raw['recorded_at'].min()
date_max        = df_raw['recorded_at'].max()
source_min      = df_raw['source_updated_at'].min()
source_max      = df_raw['source_updated_at'].max()
fuel_type_counts = df_raw['fuel_type'].value_counts().to_dict()

# ── Price statistics (on cleaned data) ────────────────────────────────────────
price_stats = {}
price_stats_raw = {}
for ft in all_types:
    sub     = df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence']
    sub_raw = df_raw[df_raw['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence']
    price_stats[ft] = {
        'count':  len(sub),
        'mean':   sub.mean(),
        'median': sub.median(),
        'std':    sub.std(),
        'min':    sub.min(),
        'max':    sub.max(),
        'p10':    sub.quantile(0.10),
        'p25':    sub.quantile(0.25),
        'p75':    sub.quantile(0.75),
        'p90':    sub.quantile(0.90),
        'iqr':    sub.quantile(0.75) - sub.quantile(0.25),
        'spread': sub.max() - sub.min(),
    }
    price_stats_raw[ft] = {
        'min': sub_raw.min(),
        'max': sub_raw.max(),
        'count_outliers': len(sub_raw) - len(sub),
    }

# ── Update lag ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df_raw['lag_hours'] = (df_raw['recorded_at'] - df_raw['source_updated_at']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600
lag_all   = df_raw['lag_hours']
lag_neg   = lag_all[lag_all < 0]
lag_clean = lag_all[lag_all >= 0]

lag_stats = {
    'neg_count':    len(lag_neg),
    'neg_pct':      len(lag_neg) / len(lag_all) * 100,
    'median_hours': lag_clean.median(),
    'mean_hours':   lag_clean.mean(),
    'p25_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.25),
    'p75_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.75),
    'p90_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.90),
    'p95_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.95),
    'max_hours':    lag_clean.max(),
}

buckets = {
    '< 1 hour':   int((lag_clean < 1).sum()),
    '1–6 hours':  int(((lag_clean >= 1) & (lag_clean < 6)).sum()),
    '6–24 hours': int(((lag_clean >= 6) & (lag_clean < 24)).sum()),
    '1–7 days':   int(((lag_clean >= 24) & (lag_clean < 168)).sum()),
    '7–30 days':  int(((lag_clean >= 168) & (lag_clean < 720)).sum()),
    '> 30 days':  int((lag_clean >= 720).sum()),
}
total_lag_recs = sum(buckets.values())

# ── Station coverage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
station_fuels      = df_raw.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].nunique()
coverage_counts    = station_fuels.value_counts().sort_index()
fuel_station_counts = df_raw.groupby('fuel_type')['node_id'].nunique()

# ── Chart helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def fig_to_b64(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode()
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64

def comma_fmt(ax, axis='y'):
    fmt = FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'{int(x):,}')
    if axis == 'y': ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(fmt)
    else:           ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(fmt)

# ── Chart 1: Box plots (main 3 fuel types) ────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.5))
box_data   = [df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence'].values for ft in MAIN_TYPES]
box_labels = [FUEL_LABELS[ft] for ft in MAIN_TYPES]
bp = ax.boxplot(box_data, patch_artist=True, notch=False,
                medianprops=dict(color='white', linewidth=2.5),
                whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.3, color='#555'),
                capprops=dict(linewidth=1.3, color='#555'),
                flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2.5, alpha=0.25, linestyle='none'))
for patch, ft in zip(bp['boxes'], MAIN_TYPES):
    patch.set_facecolor(FUEL_COLORS[ft])
    patch.set_alpha(0.82)
ax.set_xticklabels(box_labels, fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type (E10, B7 Diesel, E5)\nP1–P99 range shown; extreme outliers removed', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
for i, ft in enumerate(MAIN_TYPES, 1):
    s = price_stats[ft]
    ax.annotate(f"Med {s['median']:.1f}p", xy=(i, s['median']),
                xytext=(i + 0.35, s['median'] + 0.5),
                fontsize=8.5, color='#1e3a5f', va='center', fontweight='bold')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_boxplot = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 2: All fuel types — mean + IQR ─────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
x      = np.arange(len(all_types))
means  = [price_stats[ft]['mean']   for ft in all_types]
p25s   = [price_stats[ft]['p25']    for ft in all_types]
p75s   = [price_stats[ft]['p75']    for ft in all_types]
labels = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)   for ft in all_types]
colors = [FUEL_COLORS.get(ft, '#888') for ft in all_types]

bars = ax.bar(x, means, color=colors, alpha=0.85, width=0.5, zorder=3)
for i, ft in enumerate(all_types):
    ax.plot([i, i], [p25s[i], p75s[i]], color='#1F2937', linewidth=2.8, zorder=5)
    ax.plot([i-0.12, i+0.12], [p25s[i], p25s[i]], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.8, zorder=5)
    ax.plot([i-0.12, i+0.12], [p75s[i], p75s[i]], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.8, zorder=5)
    ax.text(i, means[i] + 0.8, f'{means[i]:.1f}p', ha='center', va='bottom',
            fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', color='#1e3a5f')

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=10, rotation=12, ha='right')
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Mean Price with IQR by Fuel Type (all types)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
low_y = min(p25s) - 8
high_y = max(means) + 15
ax.set_ylim(low_y, high_y)
iqr_line = mpatches.Patch(color='#1F2937', label='IQR (P25–P75)')
ax.legend(handles=[iqr_line], fontsize=9.5)
fig.tight_layout()
chart_mean_iqr = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 3: Price spread ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.5))
spreads = [price_stats[ft]['spread'] for ft in all_types]
iqrs    = [price_stats[ft]['iqr']    for ft in all_types]
labels  = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)  for ft in all_types]
x = np.arange(len(all_types))
w = 0.35
ax.bar(x - w/2, spreads, width=w, color='#DC2626', alpha=0.82, label='Max − Min (Full Range)', zorder=3)
ax.bar(x + w/2, iqrs,    width=w, color='#2563EB', alpha=0.82, label='IQR (P25–P75)',          zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=10, rotation=12, ha='right')
ax.set_ylabel('Pence per litre', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Spread & Market Competitiveness by Fuel Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
for i, (s, iq) in enumerate(zip(spreads, iqrs)):
    ax.text(i - w/2, s + 0.5, f'{s:.0f}p', ha='center', fontsize=8.5, fontweight='bold', color='#991B1B')
    ax.text(i + w/2, iq + 0.5, f'{iq:.0f}p', ha='center', fontsize=8.5, fontweight='bold', color='#1D4ED8')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_spread = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 4: Lag histogram ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.5))
b_edges  = [0, 0.5, 1, 2, 6, 12, 24, 48, 72, 168, 336, 720, lag_clean.max() + 1]
b_labels = ['<30m','30m–1h','1–2h','2–6h','6–12h','12–24h','1–2d','2–3d','3–7d','7–14d','14–30d','>30d']
counts_h = [int(((lag_clean >= b_edges[i]) & (lag_clean < b_edges[i+1])).sum()) for i in range(len(b_labels))]
colors_h = ['#16A34A' if i <= 1 else '#F59E0B' if i <= 5 else '#DC2626' for i in range(len(b_labels))]
ax.bar(range(len(b_labels)), counts_h, color=colors_h, alpha=0.87, zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(b_labels)))
ax.set_xticklabels(b_labels, rotation=38, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Records', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Distribution of Retailer Price Update Lag', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
comma_fmt(ax, 'y')
patches = [mpatches.Patch(color='#16A34A', label='≤ 1 hour (fresh)'),
           mpatches.Patch(color='#F59E0B', label='1h – 24h'),
           mpatches.Patch(color='#DC2626', label='> 24h (stale)')]
ax.legend(handles=patches, fontsize=9.5)
for i, v in enumerate(counts_h):
    if v > 0:
        ax.text(i, v + max(counts_h)*0.005, f'{v:,}', ha='center', fontsize=7.5, color='#374151')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_lag_hist = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 5: Lag pie ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
bv  = list(buckets.values())
blb = list(buckets.keys())
pie_colors = ['#16A34A','#22C55E','#F59E0B','#EF4444','#DC2626','#991B1B']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
    bv, labels=blb, autopct=lambda p: f'{p:.1f}%' if p > 1 else '',
    colors=pie_colors, startangle=140, pctdistance=0.80,
    textprops={'fontsize': 9.5})
for at in autotexts: at.set_fontsize(8.5)
ax.set_title('Update Lag Breakdown by Time Window', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
fig.tight_layout()
chart_lag_pie = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 6: Station coverage bar ────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
cx  = [str(c) for c in coverage_counts.index]
cy  = coverage_counts.values
gradient_colors = ['#93C5FD','#60A5FA','#2563EB','#1D4ED8','#1E3A8A','#172554'][:len(cx)]
bars = ax.bar(cx, cy, color=gradient_colors[:len(cx)], alpha=0.87, zorder=3)
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Fuel Types Reported per Station', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Stations', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Station Coverage: Fuel Type Breadth', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
comma_fmt(ax, 'y')
for bar, val in zip(bars, cy):
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + 15,
            f'{val:,}', ha='center', fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', color='#1e3a5f')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_coverage = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 7: Stations per fuel type ──────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
ft_labels = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft) for ft in all_types]
ft_counts = [int(fuel_station_counts.get(ft, 0)) for ft in all_types]
sorted_pairs = sorted(zip(ft_counts, ft_labels, all_types), reverse=True)
ft_counts_s, ft_labels_s, ft_keys_s = zip(*sorted_pairs)
bars = ax.barh(ft_labels_s, ft_counts_s,
               color=[FUEL_COLORS.get(k,'#888') for k in ft_keys_s], alpha=0.87)
ax.set_xlabel('Unique Stations Reporting', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Station Coverage by Fuel Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.xaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
comma_fmt(ax, 'x')
for bar, val in zip(bars, ft_counts_s):
    ax.text(val + 20, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
            f'{val:,}', va='center', fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', color='#1e3a5f')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_fuel_stations = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 8: Percentile profile (main 3) ─────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
pcts = [5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95]
for ft in MAIN_TYPES:
    sub  = df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence']
    vals = [sub.quantile(p/100) for p in pcts]
    ax.plot(pcts, vals, marker='o', label=FUEL_LABELS[ft],
            color=FUEL_COLORS[ft], linewidth=2.2, markersize=5.5)
ax.set_xlabel('Percentile', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Percentile Profile by Fuel Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.xaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.2, linestyle='--')
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
ax.set_xticks(pcts)
ax.set_xticklabels([f'P{p}' for p in pcts])
fig.tight_layout()
chart_percentile = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Derived values for HTML ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
e10  = price_stats['E10']
b7   = price_stats['B7_STANDARD']
e5   = price_stats.get('E5', {})
diesel_premium = b7['mean'] - e10['mean']
e10_50L_spread = e10['iqr'] * 50 / 100
e10_iqr_pounds = e10['iqr'] * 50 / 100
e10_max_spread_pounds = e10['spread'] * 50 / 100

pct_fresh     = (buckets['< 1 hour'] + buckets['1–6 hours']) / total_lag_recs * 100
pct_stale_7d  = (buckets['7–30 days'] + buckets['> 30 days']) / total_lag_recs * 100
pct_stale_30d = buckets['> 30 days'] / total_lag_recs * 100

def fp(v):  return f"{v:.1f}"
def fp2(v): return f"{v:.2f}"
def fpi(v): return f"{int(round(v)):,}"

# ── Build HTML ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
HTML = f"""<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026</title>
<style>
:root {{
  --navy:#1e3a5f; --blue:#2563EB; --green:#16A34A; --red:#DC2626;
  --amber:#D97706; --purple:#7C3AED; --orange:#EA580C;
  --light:#F0F4F8; --border:#D1D5DB; --text:#1F2937; --muted:#6B7280;
}}
*{{box-sizing:border-box;margin:0;padding:0}}
body{{font-family:'Segoe UI',Arial,sans-serif;font-size:14px;color:var(--text);background:#F8FAFC;line-height:1.6}}
.page{{max-width:1060px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 24px 60px}}

/* Cover */
.cover{{background:linear-gradient(135deg,var(--navy) 0%,#1D4ED8 100%);color:#fff;padding:52px 48px 42px;border-radius:0 0 16px 16px;margin-bottom:36px}}
.cover .label{{font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:2px;text-transform:uppercase;opacity:.7;margin-bottom:10px}}
.cover h1{{font-size:29px;font-weight:700;line-height:1.25;margin-bottom:12px}}
.cover .subtitle{{font-size:15px;opacity:.85;max-width:640px;line-height:1.6}}
.cover .meta{{margin-top:26px;display:flex;gap:28px;font-size:12px;opacity:.72;flex-wrap:wrap}}

/* KPI strip */
.kpi-strip{{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(5,1fr);gap:14px;margin-bottom:36px}}
.kpi-card{{background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:10px;padding:18px 14px;text-align:center;box-shadow:0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.05)}}
.kpi-card .kpi-val{{font-size:26px;font-weight:700;color:var(--navy);line-height:1.1}}
.kpi-card .kpi-unit{{font-size:10.5px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:2px}}
.kpi-card .kpi-label{{font-size:11.5px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:6px;line-height:1.35}}

/* Section */
.section{{background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:12px;padding:30px 34px;margin-bottom:26px;box-shadow:0 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.04)}}
.section-header{{display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:12px;margin-bottom:18px;border-bottom:2px solid var(--light);padding-bottom:11px}}
.section-num{{font-size:12.5px;font-weight:600;color:var(--blue);background:#EFF6FF;border-radius:20px;padding:3px 11px}}
.section-title{{font-size:18px;font-weight:700;color:var(--navy)}}
h3{{font-size:14.5px;font-weight:600;color:var(--navy);margin:20px 0 9px}}
p{{margin-bottom:11px;line-height:1.7}}
code{{background:#F3F4F6;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:4px;font-size:12.5px;color:#374151}}

/* Tables */
.tbl-wrap{{overflow-x:auto;margin:14px 0}}
table{{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:13.5px}}
thead th{{background:var(--navy);color:#fff;padding:9px 13px;text-align:right;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:.3px;white-space:nowrap}}
thead th:first-child{{text-align:left}}
tbody tr:nth-child(even){{background:#F9FAFB}}
tbody td{{padding:8px 13px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);text-align:right;white-space:nowrap}}
tbody td:first-child{{text-align:left;font-weight:500}}
tbody tr:hover{{background:#EFF6FF}}
.badge{{display:inline-block;padding:2px 9px;border-radius:12px;font-size:11px;font-weight:600}}
.bg{{background:#DCFCE7;color:#15803D}}.ba{{background:#FEF3C7;color:#92400E}}.br{{background:#FEE2E2;color:#991B1B}}.bb{{background:#DBEAFE;color:#1D4ED8}}.bp{{background:#EDE9FE;color:#5B21B6}}

/* Charts */
.chart-row{{display:grid;gap:18px;margin:18px 0}}
.cols-2{{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr}}
.cols-1{{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.chart-box{{background:#F9FAFB;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:10px;padding:14px;text-align:center}}
.chart-box img{{max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:6px}}
.chart-caption{{font-size:11.5px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:7px;font-style:italic}}

/* Callouts */
.callout{{border-radius:8px;padding:13px 17px;margin:14px 0;display:flex;gap:11px;align-items:flex-start}}
.ci{{background:#EFF6FF;border-left:4px solid var(--blue)}}
.cw{{background:#FFFBEB;border-left:4px solid var(--amber)}}
.cs{{background:#F0FDF4;border-left:4px solid var(--green)}}
.cd{{background:#FEF2F2;border-left:4px solid var(--red)}}
.callout-icon{{font-size:15px;margin-top:1px;flex-shrink:0}}
.callout-text{{font-size:13.5px;line-height:1.65}}
.callout strong{{font-weight:600}}

/* Findings */
.findings-list{{list-style:none;counter-reset:f}}
.findings-list li{{counter-increment:f;display:flex;gap:13px;margin-bottom:18px;align-items:flex-start}}
.findings-list li::before{{content:counter(f);background:var(--navy);color:#fff;font-weight:700;font-size:12px;min-width:27px;height:27px;border-radius:50%;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;margin-top:2px;flex-shrink:0}}
.find-title{{font-weight:600;font-size:14px;color:var(--navy);margin-bottom:4px}}
.find-desc{{color:var(--text);font-size:13.5px;line-height:1.6}}
.ftag{{font-size:10px;font-weight:600;padding:2px 8px;border-radius:10px;margin-left:7px;vertical-align:middle}}
.ftag-p{{background:#EDE9FE;color:#5B21B6}}.ftag-q{{background:#FEF3C7;color:#78350F}}.ftag-m{{background:#DCFCE7;color:#14532D}}

/* Stat pills */
.stat-row{{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px;margin:11px 0}}
.stat-pill{{background:var(--light);border-radius:8px;padding:7px 13px;font-size:13px}}
.stat-pill strong{{color:var(--navy)}}

/* Two-col */
.two-col{{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:18px;margin:14px 0}}

footer{{text-align:center;font-size:11.5px;color:var(--muted);padding:20px 0 6px;border-top:1px solid var(--border);margin-top:36px}}

@media(max-width:720px){{
  .kpi-strip{{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}}
  .cols-2{{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
  .two-col{{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
}}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="page">

<!-- COVER -->
<div class="cover">
  <div class="label">Analytical Report  ·  Energy & Consumer Markets</div>
  <h1>UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis<br>February 2026</h1>
  <div class="subtitle">A comprehensive examination of retail fuel pricing patterns across UK forecourts,
  covering price distributions, market competitiveness, and retailer reporting behaviour
  under the government-mandated open data scheme.</div>
  <div class="meta">
    <span>📅 {date_min.strftime('%d %b %Y')} – {date_max.strftime('%d %b %Y')}</span>
    <span>🏭 {total_records:,} price records</span>
    <span>⛽ {unique_stations:,} unique stations</span>
    <span>🌐 {len(all_types)} fuel types</span>
    <span>📋 Source: UK Government Fuel Finder API / fuelcosts.co.uk</span>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- KPI STRIP -->
<div class="kpi-strip">
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-val">{fp(e10['mean'])}p</div>
    <div class="kpi-unit">per litre</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Avg E10 Price<br>(Std Unleaded)</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-val">{fp(b7['mean'])}p</div>
    <div class="kpi-unit">per litre</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Avg Diesel Price<br>(B7 Standard)</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-val">{fp(e10['iqr'])}p</div>
    <div class="kpi-unit">IQR</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">E10 Typical Price<br>Band (P25–P75)</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-val">{fp(lag_stats['median_hours'])}h</div>
    <div class="kpi-unit">median lag</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Retailer Update<br>Freshness</div>
  </div>
  <div class="kpi-card">
    <div class="kpi-val">{unique_stations:,}</div>
    <div class="kpi-unit">forecourts</div>
    <div class="kpi-label">Unique Stations<br>Covered</div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 1: OVERVIEW -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">01</span>
    <span class="section-title">Dataset Overview & Coverage Summary</span>
  </div>

  <p>This analysis draws on <strong>{total_records:,} price observations</strong> across
  <strong>{unique_stations:,} unique UK forecourts</strong> reported under the government-mandated
  Fuel Finder open data scheme. Data compiled by fuelcosts.co.uk covers prices
  <strong>recorded between {date_min.strftime('%d %b %Y')} and {date_max.strftime('%d %b %Y')}</strong>,
  with retailer price updates spanning {source_min.strftime('%d %b %Y')} to {source_max.strftime('%d %b %Y')}.
  Six fuel types are present; three (E10, B7 Standard, E5) account for the substantial majority of records.</p>

  <p><strong>Data cleaning note:</strong> {outlier_count:,} records ({outlier_count/total_records*100:.1f}%) were
  identified as extreme price outliers (values outside P1–P99 per fuel type, e.g. £18.79/L for diesel)
  and excluded from distributional statistics. These appear to be data entry errors in the source feed.
  Record counts and station figures use the full raw dataset.</p>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead><tr>
      <th>Fuel Type</th><th>Records</th><th>% of Total</th>
      <th>Unique Stations</th><th>Station Coverage</th>
      <th>Raw Min (p/L)</th><th>Raw Max (p/L)</th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for ft in all_types:
    label = FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)
    rec   = fuel_type_counts.get(ft, 0)
    sta   = int(fuel_station_counts.get(ft, 0))
    pct_r = rec / total_records * 100
    pct_s = sta / unique_stations * 100
    rmn   = price_stats_raw[ft]['min']
    rmx   = price_stats_raw[ft]['max']
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{label}</td><td>{rec:,}</td><td>{pct_r:.1f}%</td>
        <td>{sta:,}</td><td>{pct_s:.1f}%</td>
        <td>{fp(rmn)}</td><td>{fp(rmx)}</td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="callout ci">
    <span class="callout-icon">ℹ️</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Geographic limitation:</strong> Station identifiers are anonymised SHA-256 hashes.
      Individual station names, brands, or geographic locations cannot be determined from this dataset alone.
      A join to the UK Fuel Finder station registry would be required for spatial or brand-level analysis.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 2: PRICE DISTRIBUTION -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">02</span>
    <span class="section-title">Price Distribution by Fuel Type</span>
  </div>

  <p>The distribution of retail prices is examined for each fuel type across all reporting stations.
  Statistics are computed on the outlier-cleaned dataset (P1–P99 per fuel type).
  Diesel (B7 Standard) commands the highest mean price at <strong>{fp(b7['mean'])}p/L</strong>,
  followed by E5 Super Unleaded at <strong>{fp(e5['mean'])}p/L</strong>, with E10 the
  most affordable at <strong>{fp(e10['mean'])}p/L</strong>.</p>

  <div class="chart-row cols-2">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_boxplot}" alt="Box plots — main fuel types">
      <div class="chart-caption">Box plots: median, IQR, whiskers (1.5×IQR) for E10, B7 Diesel, and E5 (P1–P99 range)</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_percentile}" alt="Percentile profile">
      <div class="chart-caption">Price percentile profiles (P5–P95) illustrating distribution shape for the main three fuel types</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-row cols-1">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_mean_iqr}" alt="Mean price with IQR — all fuel types">
      <div class="chart-caption">Mean price (bar) and IQR range (vertical line) for all six fuel types</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead><tr>
      <th>Fuel Type</th><th>Records (clean)</th><th>Mean (p/L)</th><th>Median (p/L)</th>
      <th>Std Dev</th><th>Min (p/L)</th><th>P25</th><th>P75</th><th>Max (p/L)</th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for ft in all_types:
    s     = price_stats[ft]
    label = FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{label}</td><td>{s['count']:,}</td>
        <td><strong>{fp(s['mean'])}</strong></td><td>{fp(s['median'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['std'])}</td><td>{fp(s['min'])}</td>
        <td>{fp(s['p25'])}</td><td>{fp(s['p75'])}</td><td>{fp(s['max'])}</td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="stat-row">
    <div class="stat-pill">E10 mean: <strong>{fp(e10['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">B7 Diesel mean: <strong>{fp(b7['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">E5 mean: <strong>{fp(e5['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">Diesel premium over E10: <strong>+{fp(diesel_premium)}p/L</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">HVO: <strong>{fp(price_stats['HVO']['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">B7 Premium: <strong>{fp(price_stats['B7_PREMIUM']['mean'])}p/L</strong></div>
  </div>

  <p>The standard deviation of E10 ({fp(e10['std'])}p/L) and B7 Diesel ({fp(b7['std'])}p/L)
  reflects genuine inter-station price variation, consistent with imperfect competition across the forecourt network.
  HVO (Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil, a renewable diesel) commands the highest average price at
  <strong>{fp(price_stats['HVO']['mean'])}p/L</strong>, though its small station count ({int(fuel_station_counts.get('HVO',0))}) limits
  statistical confidence.</p>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 3: PRICE SPREAD & COMPETITIVENESS -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">03</span>
    <span class="section-title">Price Spread & Market Competitiveness</span>
  </div>

  <p>Two metrics characterise market competitiveness: the <strong>full price spread</strong> (max minus min,
  after P1/P99 clipping) measures the widest consumer disparity in the market; the <strong>IQR</strong>
  (P25–P75 range) describes the price band that the majority of consumers actually encounter.
  The IQR is the more policy-relevant metric as it is robust to outliers.</p>

  <div class="chart-row cols-1">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_spread}" alt="Price spread and IQR by fuel type">
      <div class="chart-caption">Red: full price range (max − min, P1–P99 clipped); blue: IQR (P25–P75). Values in pence per litre.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead><tr>
      <th>Fuel Type</th><th>Clean Min</th><th>Clean Max</th><th>Spread (p/L)</th>
      <th>P25</th><th>P75</th><th>IQR (p/L)</th><th>50L Fill Saving (IQR)</th><th>Verdict</th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for ft in all_types:
    s     = price_stats[ft]
    label = FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)
    saving = s['iqr'] * 50 / 100
    if s['iqr'] <= 5:
        verdict = '<span class="badge bg">Competitive</span>'
    elif s['iqr'] <= 15:
        verdict = '<span class="badge ba">Moderate</span>'
    else:
        verdict = '<span class="badge br">Wide spread</span>'
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{label}</td><td>{fp(s['min'])}</td><td>{fp(s['max'])}</td>
        <td><strong>{fp(s['spread'])}</strong></td>
        <td>{fp(s['p25'])}</td><td>{fp(s['p75'])}</td>
        <td><strong>{fp(s['iqr'])}</strong></td>
        <td>£{saving:.2f}</td>
        <td>{verdict}</td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="callout cw">
    <span class="callout-icon">⚠️</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Consumer Impact — E10:</strong> The E10 IQR of {fp(e10['iqr'])}p/L means that
      for a typical 50-litre fill, consumers at a 75th-percentile station pay approximately
      <strong>£{e10_iqr_pounds:.2f} more</strong> than those at a 25th-percentile station.
      For B7 diesel the comparable figure is <strong>£{b7['iqr']*50/100:.2f}</strong> per fill —
      a material incentive for price-aware consumers to shop around.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="callout cd">
    <span class="callout-icon">🚫</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>B10 Bio-diesel anomaly:</strong> B10 shows an IQR of {fp(price_stats['B10']['iqr'])}p/L
      — the widest of any fuel type — but with only {price_stats['B10']['count']} records after cleaning,
      this figure should be treated with caution. The variation may reflect a nascent, illiquid market
      rather than structural competition failure.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 4: UPDATE FRESHNESS -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">04</span>
    <span class="section-title">Retailer Reporting Freshness Analysis</span>
  </div>

  <p>Update lag is defined as <code>recorded_at − source_updated_at</code>: the time between when a
  retailer last updated their price in the government feed and when that record was captured by the
  aggregation system. A short lag confirms near-real-time data; a long lag indicates that the displayed
  price may not reflect what consumers actually pay at the pump.</p>

  <div class="callout ci">
    <span class="callout-icon">ℹ️</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Negative lag artefacts:</strong> {lag_stats['neg_count']:,} records ({lag_stats['neg_pct']:.1f}%)
      show a negative lag (source_updated_at later than recorded_at), likely caused by minor clock-skew
      between the government API and the collection system, or retroactive price corrections.
      These records are excluded from all lag statistics and charts below.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="chart-row cols-2">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_lag_hist}" alt="Lag distribution histogram">
      <div class="chart-caption">Distribution of update lags: green ≤ 1h (fresh), amber 1–24h, red > 24h (stale)</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_lag_pie}" alt="Lag breakdown pie">
      <div class="chart-caption">Proportion of records by lag time window</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead><tr>
      <th>Lag Window</th><th>Records</th><th>% of Total</th><th>Assessment</th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody>
"""
assessments = {
    '< 1 hour':   ('bg', 'Fresh — near real-time'),
    '1–6 hours':  ('bg', 'Fresh — same day'),
    '6–24 hours': ('ba', 'Acceptable — within 24h'),
    '1–7 days':   ('ba', 'Marginal — 1 to 7 days'),
    '7–30 days':  ('br', 'Stale — 7 to 30 days'),
    '> 30 days':  ('br', 'Very stale — over 30 days'),
}
for k, v in buckets.items():
    bc, assess = assessments[k]
    HTML += f"""      <tr>
        <td>{k}</td><td>{v:,}</td>
        <td>{v/total_lag_recs*100:.1f}%</td>
        <td><span class="badge {bc}">{assess}</span></td>
      </tr>
"""
HTML += f"""    </tbody>
  </table>
  </div>

  <div class="stat-row">
    <div class="stat-pill">Median lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['median_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">Mean lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['mean_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">IQR: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['p25_hours'])}h – {fp(lag_stats['p75_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">P90 lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['p90_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">P95 lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['p95_hours'])}h</strong></div>
    <div class="stat-pill">Max lag: <strong>{fp(lag_stats['max_hours'])}h ({lag_stats['max_hours']/24:.0f} days)</strong></div>
  </div>

  <div class="callout cs">
    <span class="callout-icon">✅</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Headline finding:</strong> The median update lag is just <strong>{fp(lag_stats['median_hours'])} hours</strong>,
      meaning the majority of prices are updated nearly in real time. <strong>{pct_fresh:.1f}%</strong> of records
      have a lag under 6 hours, which is reassuring for the integrity of consumer-facing price comparison tools.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="callout cw">
    <span class="callout-icon">⚠️</span>
    <div class="callout-text">
      <strong>Long-tail concern:</strong> The mean lag of {fp(lag_stats['mean_hours'])} hours —
      far exceeding the {fp(lag_stats['median_hours'])}h median — reveals a right-skewed distribution.
      <strong>{pct_stale_7d:.1f}%</strong> of records have lags exceeding 7 days, and
      <strong>{pct_stale_30d:.1f}%</strong> exceed 30 days. The P95 lag of {fp(lag_stats['p95_hours'])} hours
      ({lag_stats['p95_hours']/24:.1f} days) shows the tail is non-trivial.
      These stations represent a compliance gap requiring regulatory attention.
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- SECTION 5: STATION COVERAGE -->
<div class="section">
  <div class="section-header">
    <span class="section-num">05</span>
    <span class="section-title">Station Coverage & Fuel Type Availability</span>
  </div>

  <p>Station coverage analysis examines how many fuel types each of the {unique_stations:,} stations
  reports, and which fuel types have the broadest market reach. Coverage breadth is a proxy for
  data completeness and the scheme's effective reach.</p>

  <div class="chart-row cols-2">
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_coverage}" alt="Station coverage by fuel type breadth">
      <div class="chart-caption">Number of stations by count of fuel types reported (1 = single type only)</div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart-box">
      <img src="data:image/png;base64,{chart_fuel_stations}" alt="Stations per fuel type">
      <div class="chart-caption">Unique stations reporting each fuel type</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="tbl-wrap">
  <table>
    <thead><tr>
      <th>Fuel Types Reported</th><th>Stations</th><th>% of All Stations</th><th>Interpretation</th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody>
"""
for n_fuels, count in coverage_counts.items():
    pct_s = count / unique_stations * 100
    if n_fuels == 1:
        note = "Single-type reporters — specialist sites or incomplete submissions"
    elif n_fuels == 2:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import base64
import io
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Load & clean ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df_raw = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv', parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])
df_raw['price_pence'] = pd.to_numeric(df_raw['price_pence'], errors='coerce')
df_raw = df_raw.dropna(subset=['price_pence', 'recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])

total_records_raw = len(df_raw)

# P1/P99 clip per fuel type to remove obvious data errors (e.g. 1879p/L)
def clip_outliers(sub):
    q1, q99 = sub['price_pence'].quantile([0.01, 0.99])
    return sub[(sub['price_pence'] >= q1) & (sub['price_pence'] <= q99)]

df = df_raw.groupby('fuel_type', group_keys=False).apply(
    lambda x: clip_outliers(x)
).reset_index(drop=True)

outlier_count = total_records_raw - len(df)

# ── Fuel type order & labels ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
FUEL_ORDER = ['E10', 'B7_STANDARD', 'E5', 'B7_PREMIUM', 'HVO', 'B10']
FUEL_LABELS = {
    'E10':        'E10 (Std Unleaded)',
    'B7_STANDARD':'B7 (Std Diesel)',
    'E5':         'E5 (Super Unleaded)',
    'B7_PREMIUM': 'B7 Premium Diesel',
    'HVO':        'HVO (Renewable)',
    'B10':        'B10 (Bio-diesel)',
}
FUEL_COLORS = {
    'E10':        '#2563EB',
    'B7_STANDARD':'#16A34A',
    'E5':         '#7C3AED',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#EA580C',
    'HVO':        '#0891B2',
    'B10':        '#CA8A04',
}

present_types = [f for f in FUEL_ORDER if f in df['fuel_type'].unique()]
other_types   = [f for f in df['fuel_type'].unique() if f not in FUEL_ORDER]
all_types     = present_types + other_types

# Main 3 for box plots (sufficient records)
MAIN_TYPES = [f for f in ['E10', 'B7_STANDARD', 'E5'] if f in all_types]
PREM_TYPES = [f for f in ['B7_PREMIUM', 'HVO', 'B10'] if f in all_types]

# ── Global KPIs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
total_records   = len(df_raw)
unique_stations = df_raw['node_id'].nunique()
date_min        = df_raw['recorded_at'].min()
date_max        = df_raw['recorded_at'].max()
source_min      = df_raw['source_updated_at'].min()
source_max      = df_raw['source_updated_at'].max()
fuel_type_counts = df_raw['fuel_type'].value_counts().to_dict()

# ── Price statistics (on cleaned data) ────────────────────────────────────────
price_stats = {}
price_stats_raw = {}
for ft in all_types:
    sub     = df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence']
    sub_raw = df_raw[df_raw['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence']
    price_stats[ft] = {
        'count':  len(sub),
        'mean':   sub.mean(),
        'median': sub.median(),
        'std':    sub.std(),
        'min':    sub.min(),
        'max':    sub.max(),
        'p10':    sub.quantile(0.10),
        'p25':    sub.quantile(0.25),
        'p75':    sub.quantile(0.75),
        'p90':    sub.quantile(0.90),
        'iqr':    sub.quantile(0.75) - sub.quantile(0.25),
        'spread': sub.max() - sub.min(),
    }
    price_stats_raw[ft] = {
        'min': sub_raw.min(),
        'max': sub_raw.max(),
        'count_outliers': len(sub_raw) - len(sub),
    }

# ── Update lag ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df_raw['lag_hours'] = (df_raw['recorded_at'] - df_raw['source_updated_at']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600
lag_all   = df_raw['lag_hours']
lag_neg   = lag_all[lag_all < 0]
lag_clean = lag_all[lag_all >= 0]

lag_stats = {
    'neg_count':    len(lag_neg),
    'neg_pct':      len(lag_neg) / len(lag_all) * 100,
    'median_hours': lag_clean.median(),
    'mean_hours':   lag_clean.mean(),
    'p25_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.25),
    'p75_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.75),
    'p90_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.90),
    'p95_hours':    lag_clean.quantile(0.95),
    'max_hours':    lag_clean.max(),
}

buckets = {
    '< 1 hour':   int((lag_clean < 1).sum()),
    '1–6 hours':  int(((lag_clean >= 1) & (lag_clean < 6)).sum()),
    '6–24 hours': int(((lag_clean >= 6) & (lag_clean < 24)).sum()),
    '1–7 days':   int(((lag_clean >= 24) & (lag_clean < 168)).sum()),
    '7–30 days':  int(((lag_clean >= 168) & (lag_clean < 720)).sum()),
    '> 30 days':  int((lag_clean >= 720).sum()),
}
total_lag_recs = sum(buckets.values())

# ── Station coverage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
station_fuels      = df_raw.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].nunique()
coverage_counts    = station_fuels.value_counts().sort_index()
fuel_station_counts = df_raw.groupby('fuel_type')['node_id'].nunique()

# ── Chart helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def fig_to_b64(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode()
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64

def comma_fmt(ax, axis='y'):
    fmt = FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'{int(x):,}')
    if axis == 'y': ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(fmt)
    else:           ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(fmt)

# ── Chart 1: Box plots (main 3 fuel types) ────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.5))
box_data   = [df[df['fuel_type'] == ft]['price_pence'].values for ft in MAIN_TYPES]
box_labels = [FUEL_LABELS[ft] for ft in MAIN_TYPES]
bp = ax.boxplot(box_data, patch_artist=True, notch=False,
                medianprops=dict(color='white', linewidth=2.5),
                whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.3, color='#555'),
                capprops=dict(linewidth=1.3, color='#555'),
                flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2.5, alpha=0.25, linestyle='none'))
for patch, ft in zip(bp['boxes'], MAIN_TYPES):
    patch.set_facecolor(FUEL_COLORS[ft])
    patch.set_alpha(0.82)
ax.set_xticklabels(box_labels, fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type (E10, B7 Diesel, E5)\nP1–P99 range shown; extreme outliers removed', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
for i, ft in enumerate(MAIN_TYPES, 1):
    s = price_stats[ft]
    ax.annotate(f"Med {s['median']:.1f}p", xy=(i, s['median']),
                xytext=(i + 0.35, s['median'] + 0.5),
                fontsize=8.5, color='#1e3a5f', va='center', fontweight='bold')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_boxplot = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 2: All fuel types — mean + IQR ─────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
x      = np.arange(len(all_types))
means  = [price_stats[ft]['mean']   for ft in all_types]
p25s   = [price_stats[ft]['p25']    for ft in all_types]
p75s   = [price_stats[ft]['p75']    for ft in all_types]
labels = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)   for ft in all_types]
colors = [FUEL_COLORS.get(ft, '#888') for ft in all_types]

bars = ax.bar(x, means, color=colors, alpha=0.85, width=0.5, zorder=3)
for i, ft in enumerate(all_types):
    ax.plot([i, i], [p25s[i], p75s[i]], color='#1F2937', linewidth=2.8, zorder=5)
    ax.plot([i-0.12, i+0.12], [p25s[i], p25s[i]], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.8, zorder=5)
    ax.plot([i-0.12, i+0.12], [p75s[i], p75s[i]], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.8, zorder=5)
    ax.text(i, means[i] + 0.8, f'{means[i]:.1f}p', ha='center', va='bottom',
            fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold', color='#1e3a5f')

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=10, rotation=12, ha='right')
ax.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Mean Price with IQR by Fuel Type (all types)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
low_y = min(p25s) - 8
high_y = max(means) + 15
ax.set_ylim(low_y, high_y)
iqr_line = mpatches.Patch(color='#1F2937', label='IQR (P25–P75)')
ax.legend(handles=[iqr_line], fontsize=9.5)
fig.tight_layout()
chart_mean_iqr = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 3: Price spread ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.5))
spreads = [price_stats[ft]['spread'] for ft in all_types]
iqrs    = [price_stats[ft]['iqr']    for ft in all_types]
labels  = [FUEL_LABELS.get(ft, ft)  for ft in all_types]
x = np.arange(len(all_types))
w = 0.35
ax.bar(x - w/2, spreads, width=w, color='#DC2626', alpha=0.82, label='Max − Min (Full Range)', zorder=3)
ax.bar(x + w/2, iqrs,    width=w, color='#2563EB', alpha=0.82, label='IQR (P25–P75)',          zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=10, rotation=12, ha='right')
ax.set_ylabel('Pence per litre', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Price Spread & Market Competitiveness by Fuel Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
for i, (s, iq) in enumerate(zip(spreads, iqrs)):
    ax.text(i - w/2, s + 0.5, f'{s:.0f}p', ha='center', fontsize=8.5, fontweight='bold', color='#991B1B')
    ax.text(i + w/2, iq + 0.5, f'{iq:.0f}p', ha='center', fontsize=8.5, fontweight='bold', color='#1D4ED8')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_spread = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 4: Lag histogram ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.5))
b_edges  = [0, 0.5, 1, 2, 6, 12, 24, 48, 72, 168, 336, 720, lag_clean.max() + 1]
b_labels = ['<30m','30m–1h','1–2h','2–6h','6–12h','12–24h','1–2d','2–3d','3–7d','7–14d','14–30d','>30d']
counts_h = [int(((lag_clean >= b_edges[i]) & (lag_clean < b_edges[i+1])).sum()) for i in range(len(b_labels))]
colors_h = ['#16A34A' if i <= 1 else '#F59E0B' if i <= 5 else '#DC2626' for i in range(len(b_labels))]
ax.bar(range(len(b_labels)), counts_h, color=colors_h, alpha=0.87, zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(b_labels)))
ax.set_xticklabels(b_labels, rotation=38, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Records', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Distribution of Retailer Price Update Lag', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
comma_fmt(ax, 'y')
patches = [mpatches.Patch(color='#16A34A', label='≤ 1 hour (fresh)'),
           mpatches.Patch(color='#F59E0B', label='1h – 24h'),
           mpatches.Patch(color='#DC2626', label='> 24h (stale)')]
ax.legend(handles=patches, fontsize=9.5)
for i, v in enumerate(counts_h):
    if v > 0:
        ax.text(i, v + max(counts_h)*0.005, f'{v:,}', ha='center', fontsize=7.5, color='#374151')
fig.tight_layout()
chart_lag_hist = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 5: Lag pie ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
bv  = list(buckets.values())
blb = list(buckets.keys())
pie_colors = ['#16A34A','#22C55E','#F59E0B','#EF4444','#DC2626','#991B1B']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
    bv, labels=blb, autopct=lambda p: f'{p:.1f}%' if p > 1 else '',
    colors=pie_colors, startangle=140, pctdistance=0.80,
    textprops={'fontsize': 9.5})
for at in autotexts: at.set_fontsize(8.5)
ax.set_title('Update Lag Breakdown by Time Window', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=12)
fig.tight_layout()
chart_lag_pie = fig_to_b64(fig)

# ── Chart 6: Station coverage bar ────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
cx  = [str(c) for c in coverage_counts.index]
cy  = coverage_counts.values
gradient_colors = ['#93C5FD','#60A5FA','#2563EB','#1D4ED8','#1E3A8A','#172554'][:len(cx)]
bars = ax.bar(cx, cy, color=gradient_colors[:len(cx)], alpha=0.87, zorder=3)
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Fuel Types Reported per Station', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Stations', fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Station Coverage: Fuel Type Breadth', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--', zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
